findings.text: the reader resolves the published document under $RECKON_HOME/paid-lanes.json while the observer that publishes it resolves paid_lanes.document_path() to ~/public/reckon/paid-lanes.json, so wherever RECKON_HOME is set a document the observer published is invisible to the pre-flight, which falls back to the recorded reading (probe, three arms in one process: with RECKON_HOME set the reader and writer paths diverge and the report reads window_sources {'codex': 'recorded'} with utilisation 0.11 while the writer's own fresh document sits on disk with 0.77; the same file named by RECKON_PAID_LANES_DOCUMENT is read and reports document with 0.77; both helpers agree with RECKON_HOME unset, the ambient case), the fix site (reckon/crew/paid_lanes.py document_path, out of this node's write paths) does not consult RECKON_HOME, and the deployment follow-on inherits the same HOME-based default, so the feature is inert under any RECKON_HOME deployment unless the env override is also set.

the record says the base arm's module under test was named on its header and prints header blocks for both arms, but neither /home/ITER/mcintos/.cache/reckon-preflight-gate/head2.log nor base3.log contains any revision, tree, command or module.__file__ line (a grep for revision and module.__file__ returns nothing in either file), so the round-one fix replaced a head log naming the wrong revision with two logs naming none and the 375/369 figures cannot be tied to a revision from the receipt.

the log's own header names head dfebd2b1 (log mtime 05:40) while the manifest's negative_control_note says the control was re-executed at 1928299d and the archive claims the same, so the receipt does not name the revision the record attributes to it; my own overlay recheck at 2ec95173 supplies the log's missing fact (pristine green, declared mutation red on the same absent-document assertion), so the substance holds and the receipt is mislabelled.

item_verdicts.diff: read commit by commit against base 9645fd62 -- seven paths: reckon/budget.py +172/-27 (published_document_path, _reaged, _published_fresh_windows, _merge_windows, the merge inside preflight, window_sources), reckon/cli.py and reckon/mcp.py naming budget.published_document_path(), the new 417-line test file with 7 cases, the archive evidence page, the plan page's landed paragraph, and one figure; the fix commit's _reaged re-derives age_seconds from observed_at against the moment of the read at both figure and reading level, which resolves round one's baked-age finding, and the two stale docstrings and the changelog prose it also raised are rewritten.
item_verdicts.done_when: the reviewed manifest's test_logs names a 17-file gate (head 375 passed 1 failed EXIT=1 in 294.09s; base 369 passed EXIT=0 in 665.69s) whose one failure is tests/test_ledger.py::test_every_read_view_returns_and_large_defaults_are_compact on the MCP read tool's 30 s deadline; I re-ran that case alone at the documented head (1 passed in 149.17s) and a focused selection over the changed surface's importers (138 passed EXIT=0 in 78.00s), so the gate's single failure reads as the storage-latency knife-edge rather than this change -- but the head log carries no revision header and its mtime precedes the fix commit by 29 minutes (see findings).
item_verdicts.goal: read plan section 5 (the production pre-flight reads the published paid-lanes headroom document) against the landed merge at reckon/budget.py:1509 (_merge_windows) with both production callers at reckon/cli.py:974 and reckon/mcp.py:3517; each backend is paced from a fresh published reading and otherwise from the caller's recorded window, the report names the source per backend and per group, and the node's own figure records the split -- with the caveat in the first finding below that under RECKON_HOME the published document is never found.
item_verdicts.manifest: read the same manifest a round-one review scored evidence 15 on; its measurement_module /tmp/reckon-base-loSv/reckon/budget.py is byte-identical to base 9645fd62 for budget.py (zero-line diff) inside a complete package tree, and its negative-control log and figure resolve on disk -- but the two round-two gate logs carry no revision, tree or command header at all, and the negative-control log's own header names a superseded revision, so the record's binding of its figures to revisions is not re-derivable from its receipts (see findings).
item_verdicts.write_paths: read the manifest's seven declared write paths against git diff --stat 9645fd62..2ec95173: exactly those seven paths changed, +730/-27; the shared archive page's only deletions are its two plan-commits and plan-artifacts meta lines (2 deletions, 0 content lines) and the plan page's diff is additions only (0 deletions), so both cumulative records are spliced rather than rewritten.

justifications.durability: the age re-derivation and the per-backend merge are pinned by cases that fail when the behaviour they guard is mutated (my independent overlay recheck: pristine 1 passed, declared mutation 1 failed), but the receipts' revision binding is broken and tests/test_preflight_pace.py's exact key-set assertion still depends on no ambient document covering its backends, a fragility left coupled to the unresolved path divergence.
justifications.evidence: the substantive claims reproduce independently -- my overlay of the reviewed head turns the declared mutation red on the absent-document assertion and green pristine with module.__file__ printed, the 138-case focused selection and the flake case alone pass at 2ec95173, and the recorded lint figures (base 4/2/18 = head 4/2/18, new file clean and formatted) reproduce under the pinned ruff 0.16.4 on complete trees -- but the gate logs carry no revision header (head2.log mtime 05:26 precedes the 05:55 fix commit) and the negative-control log names dfebd2b1 while the manifest claims re-execution at 1928299d, so the receipts do not establish what the record says they do.
justifications.fit: the reader reuses paid_lanes' own read path and constants and the touched docstrings now describe the merge, so round one's stale-docstring and changelog-prose findings are resolved, but one published document is resolved through two independent path helpers whose disagreement is documented in neither, a design-fit cost the deployment follow-on inherits.
justifications.goal_fidelity: the deliverable is landed and wired at both production callers with the source named per backend only when a figure exists, but the reader's RECKON_HOME branch and the writer's HOME-based default are two different resolutions of one published document, so under any RECKON_HOME deployment the pre-flight reads none and the feature is inert (see the first finding).
justifications.scope_discipline: every changed path is inside the manifest's declared write paths, the shared archive page's two deletions are only its meta-line extensions, the plan page is additions only, and the worktree is clean at the reviewed head with no branch, stash or rebase.
